verses: On the left of the way, a russet pear tree Stands there all alone,—a fit image of me. There is that princely man! O that he would come, And in my poor dwelling with me be at home! In the core of my heart do I love him, but say, Whence shall I procure him the wants of the day.

At the bend in the way a russet pear tree Stands there all alone,—a fit image of me. There is that princely man! O that he would come. And rambling with me be himself here at home! In the core of my heart I love him, but say, Whence shall I procure him the wants of the day.
